issues.message: PEC 'pec' x-extent 400µm = 4.0 cells — volume under-resolved (a PEC volume's curved/edge features need ≥5 cells; a 1-2 cell slab is realized as drawn, with walls on both faces).
PEC 'pec' y-extent 400µm = 4.0 cells — volume under-resolved (a PEC volume's curved/edge features need ≥5 cells; a 1-2 cell slab is realized as drawn, with walls on both faces).

PEC sheet pec realizes on node plane 33 of axis z, and the cells on BOTH sides of that plane carry the same dielectric (eps_r = 2.1) over 48 of its footprint nodes. The sheet is therefore buried half a cell inside the dielectric instead of lying on its interface, so the realized cavity carries half a cell of the wrong medium in series (#931; the #702 measurement was 17 % on a 127 um stack). Draw the dielectric bodies up to the sheet plane, or move the sheet to the interface. Nothing is re-sampled.

all dielectric(s) ['ptfe', 'sub'] are perfectly lossless in an open (CPML) domain. If you are measuring Q / resonance, this gives an ARTIFICIALLY infinite Q (design-guide Anti-Pattern #1, an R5 surface-metric trap) — add loss, e.g. sigma = 2*pi*f*eps0*eps_r*tan_delta. (Harmless if you are not measuring Q.)

1 conductor sheet dimension(s) are solved more than 1% off their drawn size (worst 1 listed): geometry[3] 'pec' y: drawn 600µm, nodes cover 600µm, solved as 670µm (+11.67%). OBSERVED: the node span the sheet's realized footprint covers on this run's grid, plus 0.35 of the adjacent cell at each free in-plane edge -- a PEC sheet's edge is solved that far beyond its last node (measured on this solver, both polarizations; a flat wall has no such offset). REMEDY: build the in-plane profiles with rfx.mesh_edges.edge_aware_profiles(domain, dx, sheets=[...], solids=[...]) and pass them as Simulation(dx_profile=..., dy_profile=...); a node ON the edge is not the fix. STALE IF: the footprint's node span on the run's node coordinates does not reproduce the printed numbers.

Observed conductor planes on this column are [0.0025, 0.0029000000000000002] m. Make the port ground/trace declarations agree with the realized conductor surfaces. Fringing field will be clipped → Z0 may be biased HIGH by ~0%, mesh-conv may diverge. Increase domain y-extent OR move port further from sidewall.

Coaxial port 0 (face='bottom', pin r=200 um, outer r=600 um): at its junction plane (z=2.500 mm, node 25) 24/24 nodes of the FIRST dielectric ring outside the pin (271 < r <= 371 um; lattice-based bounds, so the pin's own realized rim, at most r = 200 um + dx/sqrt(2), is excluded) carry a REALIZED PEC wall — the first registered conductor outside the pin sits at r = 282.8 um. The pin is terminated in a short by registered geometry at this plane. The assembly is PEC-OR-only: a ground sheet declared as a full plane with a dielectric 'hole' declared AFTER it stays solid (issue #589: S00 = -0.9928 at 6 GHz measured on exactly that fixture). If a clearance aperture was intended, build the conductor WITH the hole (a patterned sheet shape via add_thin_conductor, or an annular volume); if this short is the intended calibration standard, no action is needed (report-only).
